product: Cartesia — text to speech, streaming (Sonic WebSocket)

source_audio.description: No audio was submitted and no request was issued: this frame is authored to Cartesia's published WebSocket protocol documentation, not captured from the service. The done message carries no audio and no text, so no spoken or written content is involved at all.

redaction.notes: Nothing was redacted because nothing was captured. context_id holds the nil GUID — the placeholder form protocol section 4 prescribes for a correlating session identifier — because no real session exists to name.

terms.basis: docs/guides/provider-recording-protocol.md section 7 — no Output was captured. Cartesia's own verdict is permitted-with-conditions; the reason there is no real capture is the absence of a capture credential in this environment, not the terms (see the sibling audio fixture's notes)

source_schema.method: The documented field set of the server-to-client done message was read from the page pinned to the 2024-11-13 API version — the value CartesiaOptions.ApiVersion sends in the Cartesia-Version header — and corroborated against https://docs.cartesia.ai/api-reference/tts/websocket: type, done, status_code, context_id. The frame conforms to that field set, nesting and types. No vendor example payload, prose or field description was copied — only the documented field names and the literal message-type constant 'done', which is interface, not expression. Every value is our own fiction. CONFIRMED AGAINST THE LIVE SERVICE 2026-08-16: a controlled probe reproducing the shipped request — corrected only by adding the required context_id and dropping the client's half-close — carrying a wrong-path control (HTTP 404 at the handshake) and an invalid-credential control (HTTP 401 at the handshake), received seven `chunk` frames followed by a terminator keyed exactly `context_id, done, status_code, type`. The documented field set is what the service actually sends. The values remain our own fiction and the class stays `synthetic`; nothing of the vendor's output was stored.

notes: The terminator CartesiaSpeechSynthesizer stops on. `done`, `status_code` and `context_id` reach the parser as unmodelled or unread siblings, which the hand-authored {"type":"done"} this fixture retires never did. A parser that threw on an unmodelled sibling passed against that object and fails against this one. `status_code` is 200 as our own fictional value; the documented type is an integer and nothing here asserts a particular one. UPDATE 2026-08-16: the type this frame was parsed by, `CartesiaTtsControlMessage`, modelled `type` and nothing else — enough to recognise this terminator and blind to the sibling `chunk` frame that carries every byte of audio, so the client stopped correctly on a stream it had never started. It is replaced by `CartesiaTtsServerMessage`; see chunk-frame.provenance.json for the measurement. What this artifact is worth: a documented schema is what the vendor says it sends, whereas a capture is what it actually sent on one day. Re-read the source_schema URL first when this suite starts failing; the page publishes no revision marker, so a silent breaking edit is indistinguishable from no edit at all.
